title: Unify fallback coordinator and migrate regional route adapters
creator: Nora Blake
description:
Summary:
We will converge several ad-hoc fallback mechanisms and regional routing adapters into a single Fallback Coordinator service and migrate region affinity logic to a lightweight adapter layer. The goal is to remove global locks, reduce contention in the routing hot path, and make fallbacks deterministic and traceable across regions.

Scope (in-scope):
- Implement a Fallback Coordinator that exposes a compact, immutable request context and deterministic resolution order for fallbacks (capacity tier -> model variant -> region).
- Replace the current lock-heavy route selection path with a tokenized actor-queue for per-route reconciliation.
- Extract regional affinity heuristics to pluggable adapters, with a stable interface for metrics and decision tracing.
- Upgrade key dependencies used in the routing service (concurrency library, metrics client) to latest stable releases to remove known contention bugs.
- Add end-to-end tracing and per-request fallback reasoning tags for Console surface visibility.

Out of scope:
- Rewriting model variant selection logic or the policy DSL.
- Major changes to autoscaling or Dedicated control plane.

Success criteria:
- 40% reduction in P95 CPU spikes seen in routing-service during 90th percentile load window (measured on perf dashboard).
- Eliminate observed global lock contention (no countable global_lock waits in pprof traces for routing-service).
- All canary traffic uses new coordinator with 0 user-facing errors for 48h at target QPS.
- Traceable fallback reasoning appears in Console tracing and the rollout dashboard.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- We prefer a single coordinator to avoid divergent fallback states across regions; this increases the complexity of the coordinator but simplifies reasoning.
- Actor-queue per-route avoids global contention but introduces additional goroutine lifecycle costs; we mitigate by pooling and backpressure tokens.
- Regional adapters will be able to short-circuit decisions for strict affinity customers (Dedicated/VPC) to preserve isolation guarantees.

Migration plan:
1) Feature-flagged Coordinator library: implement in routing-service with all logic behind a runtime flag.
2) Unit + integration tests covering all decision branches and adapter fallthroughs.
3) Canary rollout: 5% of internal traffic -> 25% -> 100% across non-critical regions for 72h per step.
4) Swap in region adapter for Dedicated/VPC customers in a targeted list; monitor metrics and latency.
5) Turn off legacy fallback path when coordinator is stable and deprecate old code.

Testing & observability:
- Add dedicated perf test harness in CI that replays production routing traces.
- Add fallback_reason tagging to traces and structured logs.
- Add dashboard panels for coordinator queue length, per-route processing latency, and adapter miss rates.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: coordinator introduces new SLO failure modes if it becomes a single point of decisioning. Mitigation: keep coordinator stateless and horizontally scalable; implement multi-zone replicas.
- Risk: dependency upgrades may surface API incompatibilities. Mitigation: isolate upgrades behind shims and run integration tests in a staging environment that mirrors prod traffic patterns.

Rollout checklist:
- [ ] RFC reviewed by Aditya (runtime) and Priya (console)
- [ ] Security review completed (KMS/tenant isolation impact)
- [ ] Perf-run showing P95 improvement on canary cluster
- [ ] Migration playbook approved by SRE

Links:

- Perf dashboard (canary): https://metrics.redwood/routing/coordinator-canary (internal)
- Related PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/1128
